title: Adding and Scaling Vectors
short: Add tip to tail; scaling stretches or flips.

blocks.html: Since a vector is a move, combining vectors means combining moves. With components, the arithmetic happens one coordinate at a time.

$\langle a, b \rangle + \langle c, d \rangle = \langle a + c,\ b + d \rangle$: place the vectors tip to tail. $k\langle a, b \rangle = \langle ka, kb \rangle$: this stretches the length by $|k|$, and a negative $k$ reverses the direction. $\mathbf{u} - \mathbf{v} = \mathbf{u} + (-\mathbf{v})$.

Doing move $\mathbf{u}$ and then move $\mathbf{v}$ takes you as far across as both moves together, and as far up as both together, so the components add. Drawn as arrows, start the second where the first ends; the sum goes from the very start to the very end. Doing the same move twice, $2\mathbf{u}$, doubles every component.

blocks.name: vectors2d
blocks.cap: Tip to tail: the sum runs from the start of $\mathbf{u}$ to the tip of $\mathbf{v}$.

blocks.title: Lengths don't simply add
blocks.q: For the same vectors, compare $|\mathbf{u} + \mathbf{v}|$ with $|\mathbf{u}| + |\mathbf{v}|$.
steps: The sum is shorter because the two moves partly point in different directions.

blocks.html: Subtracting in the wrong order. $\mathbf{u} - \mathbf{v}$ and $\mathbf{v} - \mathbf{u}$ have the same length but point in opposite directions. Check with a sketch: $\mathbf{u} - \mathbf{v}$ is the arrow from the tip of $\mathbf{v}$ to the tip of $\mathbf{u}$ (when both start at the same point), because $\mathbf{v} + (\mathbf{u} - \mathbf{v}) = \mathbf{u}$.
